breakdown.description: The prompt replaces the unit force required for a deflection calculation with a unit moment; in the unit-load method, the virtual load must match the type and direction of the desired displacement.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly states 'apply a unit moment of 1 N·mm in the clockwise direction at x = 2000 mm to generate the moment diagram m(x),' which repeats the original error. The ground truth requires a unit force (not a unit moment) at the point of interest for a deflection calculation. The agent even attempts to justify this incorrect approach by claiming 'The clockwise unit moment assumption follows standard convention for generating auxiliary moment diagrams that correspond to downward deflections,' which is incorrect and doubles down on the error.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats simple supports as zero-rotation boundaries, even though a simply supported beam is free to rotate at its supports.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly states 'Treat the simple supports as zero-rotation boundaries in both the real and auxiliary systems,' which directly repeats the original error. A simply supported beam is free to rotate at its supports, and the ground truth removes this incorrect constraint entirely. The agent failed to correct this inconsistency.
